symptoms: Water-soaked streaks on leaf margins that turn yellow to white, starting from leaf tips and edges; caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae

treatment_option_a.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP + Streptocycline
treatment_option_a.dosage: Copper Oxychloride at 0.3% + Streptocycline (Streptomycin sulphate + Tetracycline) at 0.005%-0.01%, repeated at 10-15 day intervals
treatment_option_a.trial_result: Mean disease index of 34.7% versus 63.9% in untreated plots; grain yield reached 49.1 quintals/hectare

treatment_option_b.name: Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (alone)
treatment_option_b.trial_result: Disease control up to 76.5% with 2.67% yield increase in field trials

source: Field trial published via ResearchGate/Academia.edu (2022, Bihar); biological control review, ScienceDirect (2025)
region: Bihar, and widely reported across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal rice belts

symptoms: Pinkish larvae boring inside cotton bolls, small holes in bolls, rosette flowers; infestation typically appears 45-60 days after sowing and is hard to detect from outside

treatment_option_a.name: Pheromone Traps (Gossyplure) + Biological Control
treatment_option_a.dosage: 5 pheromone traps per hectare from 45 days after sowing; release Trichogramma bactrae parasitoid at 60,000/acre at 3-week intervals
treatment_option_a.trial_result: Reduced need for insecticide applications by 50-75% in pheromone-treated fields (published field trials, Egypt/India)

treatment_option_b.name: Emamectin Benzoate 5SG or Cypermethrin 25EC
treatment_option_b.dosage: Emamectin Benzoate @ 100g/ha, or Cypermethrin 25EC @ 80ml/10L; spray at reproductive stage when infestation crosses 5% Economic Threshold Level (ETL), repeat every 7-15 days
treatment_option_b.trial_result: Emamectin benzoate 5SG achieved 70.5% mortality in first spray; among the most effective insecticides evaluated in multi-year ICAR-CICR field trials

source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur - Official Pest and Disease Management Advisory 2024

symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions on leaves and stems, white fungal growth on the underside of leaves in humid conditions, caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans

treatment_option_a.name: Mancozeb 75% WP (prophylactic spray)
treatment_option_a.dosage: 0.25% concentration, first spray at 35 days after sowing, repeat at weekly intervals before disease onset
treatment_option_a.trial_result: Disease control efficacy around 71-77% across multi-year ICAR-CPRI field trials

treatment_option_b.name: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (curative spray)
treatment_option_b.dosage: 0.25%-0.3% concentration, applied at onset of disease symptoms, follow-up spray after 7 days
treatment_option_b.trial_result: Reduced disease severity to as low as 8.5%, with disease control up to 90.2% in ICAR-CPRI Meerut trials

disease: Rice Blast (Leaf Blast and Neck Blast)
symptoms: Diamond-shaped grey-centered lesions with brown margins on leaves (leaf blast); blackening and breaking of the neck node causing panicle death (neck blast), caused by the fungus Pyricularia oryzae

treatment_option_a.name: Kitazin 48% EC
treatment_option_a.trial_result: Reduced leaf blast incidence by 51.4% in ICAR-IIRR All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) trials, 2023

treatment_option_b.name: Isoprothiolane 40% EC
treatment_option_b.dosage: 1.5 ml/litre, foliar spray, effective against both leaf blast and neck blast
treatment_option_b.trial_result: Reduced neck blast incidence by 51% and increased yield by 31% in ICAR-IIRR AICRIP trials, 2023; untreated leaf blast severity of 52.3% caused a matching 52.3% yield reduction

source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad - Official Annual Report 2023
region: Widespread across all major rice-growing states; high intensity of neck blast reported in Kerala and Telangana (2022 survey season)
